locator.paragraph: First, continuing from previous page;61.3% denominator excludes trainees. Read with physical2 migration-route distinction.

correction: IW33/2025 studies nationality-defined employment, and expressly says most migration occurs outside the special route. Its61.3% is the share of social-insured workers excluding trainees in jobs generally requiring vocational or university education, not a route-defined estimate. But IAB2/2023physical18 independently reports just under60% of actual route users employed as skilled workers, specialists or experts. That affirmative evidence preserves the broad skilled-employment argument.
effect: Unresolved: the named source population is misdescribed, but its practical effect is limited by corroborating route-specific evidence and an outstanding exact-draft gate. No actual route share or quota effect is recalculated.
limits: Does not establish that61.3% is the actual route-specific value, that current route users lack skills, or that cutting the quota is justified. Nationality and route populations overlap. Exact current consultation draft and its date have not been obtained; do not substitute the earlier8th amendment or later enacted rule.
context_and_alternatives: All4 author pages read. The paragraph distinguishes absence of formal qualification requirements from actual skilled employment, and explicitly attributes61.3% to IW33/2025. A shorthand nationality-to-route inference or confusion with independently established roughly60% IAB results is a strong benign explanation. The original IW paper itself recommends against quota reduction, so its overall recommendation is not misrepresented.
materiality_explanation: Potentially minor source-population precision issue; the same broad policy premise has separate primary support. No material reversal of the argument is established.
